title: Component-Adaptive and Lesion-Level Supervision for Improved Small Structure Segmentation in Brain MRI (CATMIL)
mechanism: Adds a lesion-level multiple-instance term (per lesion, -log of the max probability inside it) and a component-adaptive Tversky term (voxel weight 1/(size+5)) to DiceCE, so every lesion gets a detection signal independent of size.
adaptation: Bags = crack instances after merging fragments (closing r 2-3 px, drop specks < 3 px), dilated by 2 px so one pixel anywhere on the 4 px dark line satisfies the bag (jitter tolerant); same for inactive components. lambda_MIL 0.2, MIL-only first. Targets the E1 failure where 70% of crack pixels get p < 0.001.
min_experiment: Arm: house + MIL on merged dilated crack/inactive instances (also PF variant), 5 seeds. Baseline: house and PF 5-seed. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 / relR@2; test clean-49 component recall <20 and >=20 px at relP@2 >= 0.90; crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02, or test crack IoU drop > 0.012 without relF1@2 gain.
evidence: MSLesSeg (nnU-Net): small-lesion recall 0.873 vs 0.796 DiceCE, missed lesions -48%, DSC comparable; ablation: MIL alone 0.871 (all of the gain), CAT alone 0.823 n.s.; more small FPs removed by a size filter; second dataset 3D-MR-MS same direction with more FPs.
prior_overlap: Skeleton Recall (w 1.0 / 0.1) shares the aim (thin-structure recall) but is a different mechanism; it widened predictions. MIL acts on one pixel per instance. No MIL or instance loss was run.
